cards.explanation: The answer is that Pharaoh will drive them out completely. The LORD tells Moses, Israel's leader, that after one more plague Pharaoh, Egypt's king, “…will allow you to leave this place.” And when he lets them go, “…he will drive you out completely.” This is a king who went from holding the door shut to practically shoving everybody through it, friends.

The answer is articles of silver and gold. The LORD says “…men and women alike should ask their neighbors for articles of silver and gold.” Everybody gets a part in it, not just a few. Asking a neighbor to borrow a ladder is awkward enough, so I'm glad nobody handed me this assignment.

The answer is True. The text says, “And the LORD gave the people favor in the sight of the Egyptians.” After everything Egypt has been through, that's a surprise, friends. I think it's one more sign that the LORD is the One running this whole story.

The answer is highly regarded. The text says Moses himself “…was highly regarded in Egypt by Pharaoh’s officials and by the people.” Think about that for a second, friends. After all those wonders, Pharaoh's own officials still think highly of him. I'd be thrilled if a baker still thought that much of me after one burnt batch.

The answer is False. The message says, “Such an outcry has never been heard before and will never be heard again.” So it won't sound like cries heard there before. This is a heavy part of the story, so I'll just say it plainly. The cry that comes will be like nothing Egypt has ever heard.

The answer is that not even a dog will snarl. The message says, “But among all the Israelites, not even a dog will snarl at man or beast.” Dogs love to make noise, so a quiet dog is a big deal, friends. And then, the message says, they will know the LORD makes a distinction between Egypt and Israel.

The answer is distinction. Moses says, “Then you will know that the LORD makes a distinction between Egypt and Israel.” A distinction means He sets one apart from the other. The people will see it for themselves, friends.

The answer is “Go, you and all the people who follow you!” Moses tells Pharaoh his officials will come and bow before him, saying, “Go, you and all the people who follow you!” Those are Pharaoh's own officials in that picture, and they're the ones bowing. Then, the text says, Moses left Pharaoh's presence hot with anger.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “Pharaoh will not listen to you, so that My wonders may be multiplied in the land of Egypt.” Moses and Aaron, Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14), did all the wonders before Pharaoh, and the LORD hardened Pharaoh's heart anyway. The story keeps going, friends.

The answer is the first month of their year. The LORD says, “This month is the beginning of months for you; it shall be the first month of your year.” It's a fresh start on the calendar, friends. And it's the LORD who sets it.

The answer is True. The LORD says that if a household is too small for a whole lamb, “…they are to share with the nearest neighbor based on the number of people…” So the lamb gets divided according to how many are eating. I think that makes for a very friendly night, friends.

The answer is an unblemished year-old male. The LORD says, “Your lamb must be an unblemished year-old male…” Three things, friends: no blemish, a year old, and male. I wish my dough came with instructions that clear.
The answer is False. The LORD says the lamb may come “…from the sheep or the goats.” Both are allowed, friends. The rule that matters is that it's an unblemished year-old male.

The answer is on the doorframes of their houses. The LORD says they “…are to take some of the blood and put it on the sides and tops of the doorframes of the houses where they eat the lambs.” It goes on the sides and the top of each frame. And hold onto that blood, friends, because it comes up again in a big way.

The answers are morning and burned. The LORD says, “Do not leave any of it until morning…” and “…before the morning you must burn up any part that is left over.” The meal is for that night, so the deadline hits before breakfast, and whatever's left gets burned up. I've never kept a cookie past midnight in my life, friends, so that rule would suit me fine.
The answer is haste. The LORD says, “You are to eat in haste; it is the LORD’s Passover.” They're dressed for travel, sandals on and staff in hand, so this isn't a slow dinner. Chew fast, friends.

The answer is that He will pass over that house. The LORD says, “when I see the blood, I will pass over you.” And He says no plague will fall on them to destroy them when He strikes the land of Egypt. That's why the meal is called the Passover, friends.

The answer is for all the generations to come. The LORD says they are to celebrate this day as a feast to the LORD, “…a permanent statute for the generations to come.” It's meant to be remembered, year after year, friends. Even the ones who weren't there will hear about it.

The answer is that He brought them out of Egypt on this day. The LORD says, “…on this very day I brought your divisions out of the land of Egypt.” That's His reason for the feast, friends. He adds, “You must keep this day as a permanent statute for the generations to come.”

The answer is a cluster of hyssop. Moses says, “Take a cluster of hyssop, dip it into the blood in the basin, and brush the blood on the top and sides of the doorframe.” So hyssop works like a little paintbrush, friends. A cluster of it, dipped in the basin, and the doorframe is marked.
The answer is False. Moses says, “None of you shall go out the door of his house until morning.” Once the blood is on, everyone stays put, friends. No midnight snack runs.

The answer is land. Moses says, “When you enter the land that the LORD will give you as He promised, you are to keep this service.” The LORD made a promise about a land, and Moses says the service goes with them into it. They haven't even left Egypt yet, friends, and Moses is already giving instructions for the other side. That's planning ahead.

The answer is that they bow down and worship. The text says, “Then the people bowed down and worshiped.” After hearing all of this, they go low before the LORD, friends. Sometimes that's the best answer to a big announcement.

The answer is True. The text says, “And the Israelites went and did just what the LORD had commanded Moses and Aaron.” Moses was Israel's leader, and Aaron was his brother (Exodus 4:14). The people did what was commanded, friends. But the story isn't over yet, so there's more still to come.
